correctness.rationale: Both inverse branches cover the box with Jacobian magnitude 1/2. Averaging their action on centered coordinates gives the stated row-coefficient matrix, and the diagonal stationary coordinate covariance then gives C_ij(n)=v_j(B_M^n)_ij, with v_1=1/3 and v_j=1/12 otherwise. The characteristic determinant has just the diagonal and signed cyclic permutations. A first-coordinate walk either stays at coordinate 1 or makes a full circuit of weight -2^{-(M+1)}, possibly with half-weight self-loops at intervening coordinates; this gives an independent renewal derivation of the stated resolvent and verifies the first negative lag M. The denominator's value at z=2 is 1/2, excluding cancellation, so the nonzero roots determine the limsup by the radius of convergence. Odd M can give a zero root, harmless for the radius; the positive trace supplies a nonzero root. Roots have modulus less than 1 by the characteristic equation. In the repaired theorem (/workspace/repairs/4/RESULT.md), set h=1/M and 2lambda-1=exp(hw). At h=0 the root w=-log(3)+i*pi is simple, with derivative -1; analytic continuation and conjugation give the displayed pair and hence rho_M>=1-log(3)/(2M)-O(M^-2). For a root of maximal modulus the lower bound implies |4lambda-1|>=4rho_M-1>=3-L/M. The characteristic equation gives |2lambda-1|=|4lambda-1|^(-1/(M-1)), so rho_M<=(1+(3-L/M)^(-1/(M-1)))/2=1-log(3)/(2M)+O(M^-2). This verifies the sharper repaired claim without assuming the exhibited pair are maximizers. The frozen inverse-word and finite resolvent checker was inspected; its finite checks do not prove the large-M asymptotic.
